title: Not-for-profit accounts
examples: What is the main difference between the Income and Expenditure Account and the Receipts and Payments Account?
When do we use the Income and Expenditure Account?
Can you show me an example of an item that goes on one account but not the other?

explain.say: Today we learn about two important accounts for not-for-profit groups.
The receipts and payments account tracks all the actual cash coming in and going out.

draw.text: R&P: Cash In and Cash Out

explain.say: The income and expenditure account shows the true income earned and expenses incurred in a period.

items: Expenditure: Salaries owed but not paid

explain.say: A key difference is that the I&E account adjusts for non-cash items like depreciation.
For example, if you receive a donation for next year, it is a receipt, but not income yet.

items: Donation for Next Year | N/A | Not Income

explain.say: In real life, a school club uses this to see if it made enough money to cover its yearly costs.

faq.q: Do I always prepare both accounts?
faq.a: You prepare both if the question asks for it. The R&P is for cash, and the I&E is for performance.
asks: When do I need both accounts?
Is one account more important than the other?

faq.a: An accrual is income earned or expense incurred but not yet paid or received by the date.
asks: How do I handle expenses I haven't paid yet?

faq.a: Depreciation is a non-cash expense. It spreads the cost of an asset over time, so it goes on the I&E account.
asks: Should I include wear and tear in the R&P?

faq.q: What is the difference between income and revenue?
faq.a: For these purposes, income and revenue are often used interchangeably. They both refer to money earned.
asks: Are they the same thing in this context?

faq.q: If I pay rent in advance, where does it go?
faq.a: If you pay it in advance, it is a prepayment. It reduces the expenditure in the current year's I&E account.
asks: How do I adjust for future payments?

facts: The Receipts and Payments Account only records cash transactions.
The Income and Expenditure Account records income and expenditure on an accrual basis.
Items like depreciation and prepaid expenses are adjusted for the I&E account.
The surplus or deficit calculated from the I&E account is transferred to the Balance Sheet.

quiz.say: A charity receives a grant for next year's event. Which account is affected?
quiz.show: Receipts & Payments: Yes, Income & Expenditure: No

options.show: Receipts & Payments: No, Income & Expenditure: Yes
options.say: Receipts & Payments: No, Income & Expenditure: Yes

options.show: Receipts & Payments: Yes, Income & Expenditure: No
options.say: Receipts & Payments: Yes, Income & Expenditure: No

quiz.why: The cash receipt must be recorded in the Receipts and Payments Account, but it is not income until the service is provided.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the cash actually came into the organization, so the R&P must show it.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the accounts measure different things: cash versus true performance.
wrong.2: This is wrong because even if it is not income, the cash movement must be recorded somewhere.

quiz.say: The cost of using a vehicle over a year is calculated using which account?
quiz.why: Depreciation, which spreads the cost of an asset over time, belongs in the Income and Expenditure Account.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the Balance Sheet shows assets, not the expense calculation itself.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the expense must be accounted for to show true costs.
wrong.3: This is wrong because R&P only records actual cash payments, not accounting allocations.

quiz.say: If salaries are earned but not paid until next year, how is this treated?

options.show: The expense is ignored until paid.
options.say: The expense is ignored until paid.

quiz.why: The expense is recognized in the I&E account when it is incurred, even if the cash payment happens later.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the expense is real and must be shown in the I&E account.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the R&P account only records cash movements, not obligations.
wrong.2: This is wrong because ignoring it misrepresents the true financial performance for the current period.
